why: (a) two different APIs a reader reaches separately: the available-statuses lookup (with its admin dropdown mirror and duplicate Canceled/Cancelled values) versus the PUT /api/return edit guards on decided returns

children.subject: Return available-statuses offers both Canceled and Cancelled, mirrored in the admin status dropdown
children.question: Which statuses does GET /api/return/{id}/available-statuses offer for each return status?
children.body: Observed on Return module 3.1003 (PR build). GET /api/return/{id}/available-statuses returned: New -> [New, Completed, Canceled, Processing, Cancelled]; Requested -> [Requested]; Draft -> [Draft]; Approved -> [Approved, Completed, Processing]; PartiallyApproved -> [Completed, Processing, PartiallyApproved]; Rejected -> [Rejected]; Cancelled -> [Canceled, Cancelled]; a legacy Completed return without decided lines -> [New, Completed, Canceled, Processing, Cancelled]. The admin status dropdown shows the same list. On a cancelled return the Status dropdown and the Returns 'All statuses' filter show both values, and in translation they are indistinguishable (de Storniert twice, ru Отменён twice). Saving Completed -> New and New -> Completed in the admin UI both persisted.

children.subject: PUT /api/return on a decided return discards decision changes with a 200
children.question: What happens to decision fields sent in a PUT /api/return on an already decided return?
children.body: On a decided return, PUT /api/return changing approvedQuantity, itemState, line quantity or decline reasons returns 200 and the stored decision is unchanged (the fields are discarded without an error); moving to Approved/Requested/Cancelled or adding/removing a line returns 400 with a message. On a Requested return a PUT that raises a line quantity within the order's availability returns 200 and changes the buyer's requested quantity with no notification; above availability it is 400 'LineItem ... has incorrect quantity'. Moving a decided return to Processing and then Completed keeps the released quantities.

children.subject: Deleting a configured barcode property and reindexing stops barcode scans matching its value
children.question: What happens to barcode scans on a field whose catalog property is deleted?
children.body: vcst, Catalog 3.1046 (PR 909 build), event-based indexation off: with barcode fields = [a Product ShortText property], xAPI products(filter: ... barcode:'<value>') returns 1 hit; after DELETE /api/catalog/properties?id=<id>&doDeleteValues=true (204) and POST /api/search/indexes/index for that product (200), the same query returns totalCount 0 within about 5-10 s, with no errors[]. The store setting still lists the field, and the dedicated barcode fields GET still lists it, while the /fields list no longer contains the property; re-PUT of the same selection returns 400. On a store whose only configured barcode field was the deleted property, the response still listed the deleted field as a filter with isGenerated true, and a GTIN that exists on a product also returned 0.

children.subject: Store update and property delete reject id-in-path routes with 405
children.question: What are the correct REST route shapes for updating a store and deleting a catalog property?
children.body: DELETE /api/catalog/properties/{id} (id in path) answers 405, and PUT /api/stores/{id} answers 405 — store update is PUT /api/stores with the whole store body; Catalog.Search.BarcodeSearchFields is a Json-typed setting whose value is a JSON string.

children.subject: A Customer-scope shared wishlist is Forbidden via wishlist(listId) and missing from the recipient's own lists
children.question: Does a target organization member get the Customer-scope shared list through wishlist(listId) or wishlists?
children.body: With a wishlist whose sharingSetting is scope Customer, access Read, and a single target equal to the member's active organization, a buyer of that organization gets errors[Access denied., code Forbidden] with data.wishlist null from wishlist(listId), and the list is absent from that buyer's own wishlists(). A member of a different organization gets the same Access denied. Observed on the multi-target sharing build (sharingSetting.targets[] / addSharedWithIds, vc-module-x-cart 3.1037.0-pr-141, vc-module-cart 3.1011.0-pr-194) on a share created through the storefront; the same denial was observed on the older single sharedWithId model.

children.subject: Target organization members read a Customer-scope shared list through its sharing link
children.question: How does a target organization member read a wishlist a sales rep shared with scope Customer?
children.body: The target organization's member does get read access to a Customer-scope list, through sharedWishlist(sharingKey) (access Read, isOwner false, current message); members of each targeted organization opened /shared-list/<key> and saw the list with 'Recommended by your sales representative', while a removed organization's member got /403. The member's wishlists() is not necessarily totalCount 0 or free of non-owner lists: it returned an Organization-scope list of the member's own organization with isOwner false, while the Customer share was absent.

children.subject: On /search?barcode= the first barcode value wins and a q keyword is ignored
children.question: What does /search?barcode= do when the URL repeats barcode or also carries q?
children.body: Observed on a vc-frontend build carrying the barcode scanner search setup (theme PR 2501 over x-catalog PR 113 and catalog PR 909), store barcode fields configured. /search?barcode=<A>&barcode=<B> does not crash and logs no console error: the first value wins (a shared-GTIN A listed its 3 products even though B alone opens one product). /search?barcode=<single-hit value>&q=<unrelated term> still opens the product page, so the keyword is suppressed while a barcode is present; on a 0-hit barcode with q, Reset search navigates straight to /catalog with both barcode and q cleared, and Back returns to the barcode URL (one history step).
